title: Alice V. Cooper (97) of Champaign - thexradio.com
content:
Published on October 9, 2026 6:59 pm 
Last Updated on October 9, 2026 7:01 pm Alice V. Cooper, 97, of Champaign, Illinois formerly of Philo, Illinois passed away peacefully Monday, September 28, 2026, at Bickford Senior Living in Champaign, Illinois. Alice was born July 30, 1929, in Cumberland County, Illinois the daughter of Tracy F. And Elsie (Myers) Shull. She attended school in Montrose, Illinois.  Alice married Lowell Cooper on August 31, 1946, in Toledo, Illinois and they began their life together in rural Neoga, later moving to Philo, Illinois near Champaign.  Lowell and Alice both loved God and realized early that they needed Him to be the head of their home.  They gave their hearts to Him in Christian Baptism, at Toledo Christian Church in early 1950, worshiping and serving Him during their lives together.  After moving to Philo, they became members of the Sidney Christian Church and continued to serve God and others during their years together.  Mr. Cooper sadly passed away December 22, 2025. Alice is survived by her son, Marvin L. Cooper and wife Kathy of Decatur, Illinois; one daughter, Marilyn Warren of Philo, Illinois; grandchildren, Lyndal Cooper of Golden Valley, Arizona, Kenneth Cooper of Decatur, Illinois, Kevin Cooper and wife Dawn of Decatur, Illinois, Jeanette Trujillo of Decatur, Illinois, Angela Wease and husband Chuck of Urbana, Illinois, Andrew Warren and wife Kimberly of Philo, Illinois; 21 great grandchildren and 10 great great grandchildren. Mrs. Cooper was preceded in death by her parents; husband, Lowell; brothers, Elyza, Clifford, Joseph and Daniel: sisters, Zella, Mabel, Lucy and Cleo. As per her request, Cremation Rites will be accorded and there will be a graveside service held at 1:30 PM Saturday October 17, 2026 in the Long Point Cemetery of Neoga Township, Illinois. title: Is New Zealand v Australia on TV? Channel, kick-off time and how to watch Bledisloe Cup clash - Yahoo Sports
content: New Zealand and Australia meet in the first of back-to-back Bledisloe Cup clashes with the two rivals colliding in Auckland. The All Blacks have held the trans-Tasman prize since 2002 but hopes are high that the Wallabies can challenge them after a significant success against South Africa in their last outing. To do so, though, they will have to conquer Eden Park – a ground at which the hosts have not been beaten since 1994. With these two due to be pool stage opponents at the World Cup in a year's time, it could be a contest with greater significance. New Zealand vs Australia is due to kick off at 7.10am BST on Saturday 10 October at Eden Park in Auckland. Viewers in the United Kingdom can tune in via Sky Sports, with a live stream available via Sky Go. Damian McKenzie starts at fly half for New Zealand after Richie Mo'unga joined Ruben Love on the injury list. Beauden Barrett therefore begins at full-back, with younger brother Scott returning in the second row for his first appearance of the year after back surgery. Codie Taylor captains the side in the absence of Ardie Savea, while Shannon Frizell is primed for a first appearance since the 2023 Rugby World Cup final off the bench. title: Vietnam’s V Studios Seals Multiple Deals On ‘Red Woman’ Including Sales To North America & Japan - Deadline
content:
EXCLUSIVE: V Studios, the Vietnamese production arm of Korean exhibitor CJ CGV, has closed multiple deals on supernatural fantasy Red Woman, including sales to NewGates Corporation for Japan and Mockingbird Pictures for the US and Canada. The film, which is V Studios’ first fully in-house produced feature, has also gone to Infinity Entertainment for Australia & New Zealand; NK Contents for South Korea; and Westec Media for Cambodia. V Studios, which was previously known as V Pictures and launched here at Busan two years ago, also handles international sales for a slate of films it has invested in, as well as third-party titles. Since launch, the company has handled films including horror hits Ma Da: The Drowning Spirit, The Corpse and The Corpse 2. Starring Minh Hang, Red Woman reimagines a figure from Vietnamese folk history, the eponymous and elusive ‘Red Woman’, a character that has primarily existed through Vietnamese oral culture and collective memory. Directed by Jack Carry On, the film is fully produced by V Studios with Tam Tuong on board as executive producer. The film marks Minh Hang’s return to cinema after a three-year hiatus, following previous theatrical titles including Sweet Trap and Sister Sister 2. She also starred in Naked Truth (2022), which was streamed in Southeast Asia by Netflix. The cast also includes Rima Thanh Vy (Furies), Nhat Kim Anh (The Musician At The Dragon Citadel), Khuong Le (Meet Me At The Eclipse), Phat La and Dai Nghia. Theatrical release in Vietnam is scheduled for November 27, 2026, followed by an international rollout. V Studios said: “For generations, Vietnamese children have grown up hearing warnings about ‘Red Woman’ – a mysterious woman said to take children away if they wandered too far or disobeyed their parents. Yet unlike many established figures in Asian mythology, Red Woman has no definitive appearance, mythology or widely accepted origin story. That absence gives the filmmakers an unusual opportunity: to transform a familiar cultural fear into an entirely original cinematic mythology. “At the heart of Red Woman is a deceptively universal proposition: What would you be willing to sacrifice to get the one thing you desire most? When people reach the deepest point of desperation, resentment or longing, Red Woman appears. Possessing seemingly limitless powers, she offers them the one wish they have always wanted fulfilled. But every miracle carries a price.” Vietnamese genre cinema has recently been on a roll with a string of hits including Crimson Snout (Quy Cau), Ma Da: The Drowning and The Sisters (Cam) demonstrating local audiences’ appetite for stories drawing on folk beliefs and culturally specific supernatural imagery. title: Glasgow v Connacht: Five takeaways as Irish ‘mauled to death’ and Bundee Aki suffers another ‘lippy’ outburst - Planet Rugby
content: Connacht's Bundee Aki and, inset, Dan and Stuart Lancaster After a deserved 36-19 win for Glasgow over Connacht in Friday night’s URC fixture at Scotstoun, Planet Rugby selects five takeaways from the round three action. 19 weeks after these clubs clashed at Scotstoun in a tense URC quarter-final that was won 33-21 by the hosts, Glasgow prevailed again in stormier conditions. That balmier late May clash was a match-up between the league’s first- and eighth-placed sides following the end of the 2025/26 regular season. Here, with two rounds completed in the new campaign, it was fifth hosting 10th, but the outcome was the same as five months ago. It was no surprise – it was at Firhill way back in September 2010 when Connacht last won away to Glasgow, so this latest outcome was merely adding another L to an already lengthy list of deflating results, only this time the visitors were mauled to death as four of the five Glasgow tries stemmed from the maul. The Warriors were forced into a pre-match reshuffle. With the ill Kyle Rowe dropping out, originally selected scrum-half Jamie Dobie switched to the wing and George Horne was promoted from the bench. Connacht started the brighter and while two penalties given up at the breakdown were an initial frustration in the opposition 22, there was no stopping Sean Jansen in the 16th minute on second phase after an offside penalty against Dan Lancaster. An off-feet ruck intervention, though, from Mack Hansen provided Glasgow with their first invite into the visitors’ 22 and the situation ended with Gregor Hiddleston’s 20th minute unconverted maul try. A scrum penalty win booted down the touchline was the prompt for the even meatier maul that produced their follow-up try 13 minutes later, a 30-plus seconds shunt travelling from about 18 metres out and leaving Rory Darge celebrating the converted score and a 12-7 lead. It got better before the interval for the Darge-inspired Warriors. A third Connacht infringement in quick succession resulted in Sam Illo’s sin-binning, and the outcome was Hiddleston touching down off a maul bolstered by several backs joining. This 12-point, 19-7 point gap soon widened when successive Lancaster and Dobie kicks left Josh McKay claiming the bonus-point try on 43 minutes, but the 26-7 advantage was trimmed four minutes later with Josh Ioane finishing a lengthy Connacht attack. It meant the sin bin period ended 14-7 to Glasgow, and the riposte clearly awoke Ioane’s attacking senses as he was racing over again in the 60th minute for an unconverted try that left it 26-19. Connacht’s comeback, though, was swiftly wrecked by the carded Josh Murphy’s lack of a wrap tackling Seb Stephen. Down a forward, what developed was predictable as Glasgow kicked to the corner and mauled over for Stephen’s 65th-minute try. Fourteen points up, the hosts complicated things with a 73rd minute yellow card for Scott Cummings. But having clung on for a draw last weekend against Ulster when finishing with 13 players, they had good practice in this situation and they saw out the danger without conceding any bonus points. This was helped by Bundee Aki’s penalised verbal outburst to the referee, and then Lancaster’s clock-in-the-red penalty kick. Peter O’Mahony reveals the coach he would choose over ‘different animal’ Rassie Erasmus This match’s video analysis won’t be an easy watch for new Connacht scrum coach Trevor Woodman and John Muldoon, their lineout and maul/forwards coach. Woodman, the 2003 Rugby World Cup-winning prop with England, was recruited from Gloucester for this season, but his scrum conceded six penalties in last weekend’s plucky heist at Benetton with Francois van Wyk and Finlay Bealham as its starters, and the coughing up of two more in quick succession at Scotstoun was another wounding episode. Connacht were still 7-5 ahead when loosehead Billy Bohan was penalised on opposition ball, and with tighthead Illo penalised two minutes later on his team’s own feed, the die was cast for the Glasgow power surge that was two more maul tries before the interval to add to the one that had already got them on the board. Yes, the maul law tweak has certainly enhanced the odds for the attacking team, but the concession of a hat-trick of maul tries by Connacht in a 24-minute first-half spell that also featured a prop getting sin-binned defending a maul at his try line was bruising. There was a second-half response, Connacht stealing lineouts on 53 and 63 minutes to prevent Glasgow setting up mauls near the line, and the scrum held its own. That showed they could temporarily fix things on the run, but too much damage had already been done. There was then further pain with Glasgow scoring their fourth maul try after Connacht decided not to contest the lineout. It was the final blow, and the accompanying irony was that Connacht then failed to profit when a man up later on as they collapsed their own maul when moving forward towards the line. Ex-Ireland coach’s verdict on World Rugby’s ‘striking feature’ problem after Leinster ‘taken to the woodshed’ You would think the public humiliation of copping a four-match ban earlier this year for verbally abusing the match officials would result in Aki buttoning it on the pitch and keeping schtum no matter his perceived injustice. That punishment cost the midfielder his spot in the Ireland Six Nations squad, but Friday’s evidence was that teaching the 36-year-old a lesson isn’t an easy thing. Just minutes remained at Scotstoun with Connacht frantically trying to engineer the converted try that would have potentially earned their two bonus points – one for scoring four tries and another for losing by seven points. However, Welsh referee Ben Breakspear lost his patience with the Test-level veteran. With the Irish side trying to wrinkle some space to work the ball not far inside the Glasgow half, the official warned Aki and followed up at a breakdown with a caution that he would penalise him if he chatted to him again. Surely that was the prompt to zip it, but Aki continued his verbals and Breakspear whistled up to award a penalty to Glasgow rather than allow the play to continue with Hansen just having carried to a ruck about 10 metres inside the opposition half. That one shrill of the whistle ended Connacht’s hopes of securing any reward from their travels, and some harsh words must be doled out to Aki in the changing room for his latest unprofessional incident. Brian O’Driscoll reveals Ciaran Frawley ‘request’ which contradicts ‘narrative’ after high-profile Leinster exit Friday was Connacht boss Lancaster’s 57th birthday, but it won’t be fondly remembered by the ex-England coach as the celebration was ruined by his son Dan being on the winning Glasgow side. They had apparently not spoken to each other this week, and even a meet-up on Thursday for dinner was bereft of rugby chat, but what materialised the following night left the out-half son with all the bragging rights. So much of the hype in this fixture’s lead-up had been about how new Connacht signing Ciaran Frawley delivered to help the Irish team win last weekend in Italy, but he was eclipsed in Scotland by Lancaster Jnr and the Irishman’s troubled outing was summed up by a terrible pass under pressure flying into touch in the dying minutes. That will hurt Frawley, especially as Lancaster didn’t have much to do to outshine him on a night that was made for forwards – as seen in Glasgow’s four maul tries. Despite the greasy conditions, the 25-year-old Scotland A international played a critical part in an early contender for try of the season. He had started the second half with a probing touch finder off his left foot, and he soon followed that with a peerless right-footed cross-kick into Dobie’s breadbasket and the winger’s grubber allowed McKay to go haring in for his score. So good was that combination that Lancaster’s next involvement was softly knocking on the Connacht restart kick, resulting in the scrum that eventually led to an Irish try back, but that smudge really couldn’t dilute the brilliance of the previous cross-kick. Want more from Planet Rugby? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for world-class coverage you can trust. A Glasgow feature in the opening two rounds was their slow starts. They found themselves 0-10 down at Munster on September 26 before they managed to find an attacking pulse, and that annoyance was repeated last weekend when they hosted Ulster. Again, they conceded the opening try and were left trailing 0-7 and 7-12 before raising a proper gallop. Hopes for getting their lift-off right at the third time of asking against Connacht weren’t helped by an initially shaky lineout, and their defence was forced to absorb a copious amount of pressure in the 22. This eventually resulted in them giving up the opening try, a converted effort from close range following cumulative infringements. Glasgow’s response was swift, as they were scoring down the other end just three minutes later, but better teams than the trio of Irish sides they have started the season against will surely inflict costlier damage on Franco Smith’s team if the coach doesn’t come up with a ruse to shake up his slumbering starters. title: Section V football live updates scores, highlights for Friday, Week 6 - Democrat and Chronicle
content: Week 6 arrives with the postseason drawing closer and several high-profile matchups on the schedule across Section V. Every win carries added significance this time of year, especially for teams chasing league titles, higher playoff seeds and momentum entering the final weeks of the regular season. Fans can expect ideal football weather, with temperatures near 60 degrees at kickoff and falling into the 50s as the night progresses. We'll have scores, highlights, standout performances and updates from around the Rochester region throughout the evening as another important week of Section V football unfolds. East Rochester/Gananda rallied to defeat Penn Yan/Dundee 17-14 and improve to 3-3. Owen Munding rushed for 107 yards and threw two touchdown passes to lead the comeback. Penn Yan/Dundee fell to 4-2. Brody Pusateri threw three touchdown passes to Dayshawn Preston as Pittsford handed Hilton its first loss of the season with a 21-14 victory. The Panthers improved to 5-1, while the Cadets fell to 5-1. Mason Scott scored on a 3-yard touchdown run with eight seconds remaining, then powered into the end zone for the winning two-point conversion as Brockport rallied past Honeoye Falls-Lima 29-28. The Blue Devils improved to 4-2, while the Cougars fell to 3-3. Tyler Reger was ruled out of bounds making a fourth-down catch, turning the ball over to Pittsford with 1:24 remaining in the fourth quarter. Mason Scott capped a 72-yard touchdown drive with a 3-yard run to pull Brockport within one point with eight seconds remaining. After a penalty on the extra-point attempt, the Blue Devils elected to go for two, and Scott powered into the end zone to give Brockport a 29-28 lead. Brody Pusateri connected with Dayshawn Preston for their third touchdown of the game, with Preston breaking a tackle on the play to give Pittsford a 21-14 lead over unbeaten Hilton with 11:52 remaining in the fourth quarter. Benny Feinberg capped a 57-yard touchdown drive that took more than seven minutes with a rushing score, giving Honeoye Falls-Lima a 28-21 lead over Brockport with 1:37 remaining in the fourth quarter. Mason Scott connected with Giuseppe Marrocco for a 64-yard touchdown pass on the first play of Brockport's possession, tying the game at 21 with 8:55 remaining in the fourth quarter. Benny Feinberg bought time on fourth down before finding Chase Harrison in the back of the end zone for a touchdown. Harrison got his feet down to give Honeoye Falls-Lima a 21-14 lead early in the fourth quarter. Calvin Starwald scored his second rushing touchdown of the game to pull Hilton even with Pittsford at 14 with 3:38 remaining in the third quarter. A long kickoff return by Jared Wade gave the Cadets excellent field position. Luciano Gingello forced a late fumble that Porter Pittman recovered to help Greece Arcadia hold off Greece Olympia/Odyssey 30-29. Quarterback Jackson Child completed 10 of 16 passes for 210 yards and two touchdowns, both to Drake Sapp, who finished with six catches for 177 yards. Elijah Truesdell added 81 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 13 carries. Brody Pusateri connected with Dayshawn Preston for their second touchdown of the game, giving Pittsford a 14-7 lead over unbeaten Hilton with 6:35 remaining in the third quarter. The Panthers scored after forcing the Cadets to punt. East/World of Inquiry held off McQuaid, sealing the victory with a late interception. John Mobley Jr. rushed for two touchdowns, while Taye Brown Jr. added a 69-yard touchdown run for the Eagles. title: The Next Honda CR-V Hybrid Is Reportedly Running Late, and So Is Honda’s Plan for a Cheaper Hybrid - Yahoo Autos
content: Honda's redesigned CR-V hybrid will start mass production in the United States in May or later, months behind plan, Japan's Nikkei business daily reported on Oct. 7, Tokyo time. Nikkei said the slip covers Honda's next-generation hybrid vehicles in North America, in both the U.S. and Canada. That puts a delay on the best-selling vehicle Honda has, at the moment Honda's post-EV business plan needs it to arrive cheaper to build than the one it replaces. Honda had not posted a statement or announcement about the timing on its U.S. or global newsrooms as of Wednesday. Nikkei's story, filed from New York by Azusa Kawakami, said Honda will push back mass production of its next-generation hybrids in North America by several months. A photo caption on the story, showing a CR-V at Honda's Indiana plant, said U.S. production of the SUV's hybrid version is expected to slip to May or later. Those hybrids are the centerpiece of the plan Honda laid out at its May 14, 2026 business briefing, where it scaled back EV spending and moved money and engineers toward hybrids. Honda said that starting in 2027 it would begin launching next-generation hybrid models built on both an all-new hybrid system and an all-new platform, with 15 such models globally by the end of the fiscal year ending March 31, 2030, primarily in North America. It set two engineering targets for that system: a cost reduction of more than 30% compared with the hybrid system it introduced in 2023, and a fuel-economy gain of more than 10%. The same briefing committed the North American factories to the shift. Honda said it would reassign all excess capacity at its Ohio auto plants to gasoline and hybrid vehicles, make every auto plant in North America capable of building hybrids, and convert part of the EV battery lines at L-H Battery Company, its joint venture with LG Energy Solution, to hybrid batteries. The Auto Wire covered the pressure that put on Ohio in our look at Honda's flexible Ohio line running out of room. A 30% cost cut on a hybrid system does not arrive as a running change. Honda describes the savings as coming from an all-new hybrid system paired with a next-generation platform and a newly developed electric all-wheel-drive unit. Hardware on that scale goes into production only when a new model launches, because the body, mounts, wiring and crash structure have to be engineered around it. Until the next CR-V hybrid starts rolling, every CR-V hybrid Honda builds carries the current system, the one Honda says its successor will undercut by more than 30%. Volume is what makes that expensive. Honda's Oct. 1 sales release put third-quarter CR-V sales at a record 110,730, up 16.6%, with hybrids at 53% of the mix and 59,668 hybrid units in the quarter. That is roughly 20,000 CR-V hybrids a month in the U.S. alone. Each month the launch slides is another month of that volume built at the old cost, which feeds straight into the cost work Honda has already been pressing on suppliers, as The Auto Wire reported on Honda's supplier cost-cutting push and in our explainer on the cost overhaul. Model changeovers also have a cost that never appears on a press release. When a plant switches generations, it runs pilot builds, retools the body shop and ramps up line speed over weeks, and output dips while it does. Moving the start date moves that dip, and suppliers keep building current-generation parts longer than scheduled. The current CR-V is not a model Honda is trying to clear out. The same sales release said CR-V hit those records while overcoming a supply of 17 days, and American Honda's vice president of auto sales, Lance Woelfer, said in it, "While we are experiencing some inventory issues due to sustained strong demand, I'm proud of our production team in North America along with our dealers for continuing to focus on meeting the needs of our customers." Seventeen days of supply means a dealer selling 30 CR-Vs a month has about 17 on the ground. That suits Honda's margins and frustrates shoppers who want a specific trim and color. A later changeover keeps the current CR-V's plants building it at full tilt for longer, which helps supply in the near term. The risk sits in spring, when plants begin switching over and output dips during the ramp while demand for the outgoing model is still strong. Honda's 2026 North American manufacturing factbook, dated June 17, lists three plants building the CR-V and CR-V hybrid: the East Liberty Auto Plant in Ohio, rated at 240,000 vehicles a year and also home to the Acura MDX; Plant 2 in Alliston, Ontario; and the Indiana Auto Plant in Greensburg. A 2025 Civic hybrid hatchback in Stuttgart. In North America, Honda builds the Civic hatchback only in Greensburg, Indiana. Photo: Alexander Migl via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0) Greensburg builds just two nameplates. Honda's factbook lists it at 250,000 vehicles a year and 2,600 employees, building the Civic Hatchback, the Civic Hatchback hybrid, the CR-V and the CR-V hybrid. It is the only Honda plant in North America the factbook lists as building the Civic hatchback; the Civic sedan, Si and sedan hybrid come from Alliston's Plant 1. Honda first said it would build Civic hybrids in Indiana in an October 2023 announcement. The next Civic was supposed to make that plant busier still. In March 2025, Reuters reported that Honda had decided to build its next-generation Civic hybrid in Indiana starting in May 2028 instead of in Guanajuato, Mexico, starting in November 2027, at about 210,000 units a year, as Indianapolis station WISH-TV relayed at the time. Honda did not confirm the plan; its spokesperson told Reuters only that the company would keep weighing demand and the business environment in production decisions. By The Auto Wire's math, 210,000 Civics in a plant rated for 250,000 would leave about 40,000 slots a year for everything else Greensburg builds, CR-V included. The 2025 plan therefore always implied moving a large share of Indiana's CR-V output somewhere else, adding capacity in Greensburg, or both. Honda has not said publicly whether the next Civic is still headed to Indiana, and reports this week that the company has dropped that plan could not be confirmed against any Honda document as of Wednesday. If the Civic is not coming, Greensburg's future rests even more heavily on a CR-V whose new generation is now running late. Tariffs are why the address matters. Under the executive order implementing the U.S.-Japan agreement, signed Sept. 4, 2025, Japanese passenger vehicles carry a combined duty of 15%. A Civic built in Indiana carries none of that, and one built outside the U.S. is a tariff question Honda has to answer model by model. That calculation runs through Honda's recent U.S. plant spending, including its $472 million Alabama expansion. Honda's next quarterly earnings report is the first place the company could put a date on the next CR-V or address Greensburg's model plan in its own words. Until it does, the May timing remains Nikkei's reporting, not a Honda commitment. Shoppers can track CR-V days' supply in Honda's monthly sales releases. If it stays near 17 days through winter, expect little room to negotiate on a current CR-V hybrid and longer waits for specific trims. Anyone who wants the new hybrid system's promised 10%-plus fuel-economy gain is likely looking at summer 2027 before dealers have them in volume, if production starts in May. The current CR-V hybrid's system has been on the road since the 2023 model year, so owners and independent shops already know its parts and repair procedures; the next one will start with none of that track record. For Greensburg's 2,600 workers, the date to watch is when Honda names the plant's next-generation products. Its June factbook lists two nameplates there, and the newer of them is the vehicle whose replacement just slipped. If you need a CR-V hybrid in the next six months, are you buying the proven current model now, or waiting for the cheaper-to-build redesign and whatever teething problems come with a first-year hybrid system? title: Arsenal v Leeds Match Preview: Team News, Predicted Lineup and Score Prediction - Yahoo Sports
content: Arsenal finally return to Premier League action on Saturday lunchtime when they welcome unbeaten Leeds United to the Emirates Stadium. The Gunners went into the extended international break on the back of a painful 3-0 defeat at Brighton, which ended their perfect start to the season and left them second in the table. Leeds, meanwhile, have quietly made an excellent start. Daniel Farke's side sit just three points behind Arsenal after five matches and are yet to lose in the league, while conceding only three goals. That should ensure there is no room for complacency from Mikel Arteta's players after what happened at the Amex. The international break created several fresh concerns, although there has also been some welcome news for Arteta. According to Arsenal's official team news update, Christos Tzolis will miss the game with a muscle injury and is expected to be out for a few weeks. Kai Havertz and Ezri Konsa are set to be assessed before the match, while Declan Rice also needs careful management following his heavy workload. There is better news defensively. Ben White, Cristhian Mosquera and Piero Hincapie have all returned to training. With Tzolis missing and Havertz doubtful, this could be Viktor Gyokeres' opportunity to lead the attack. The Swede returns from an excellent international break in which he made Nations League history, having again demonstrated that he will score when a team plays to his strengths. Leeds are without some key players ahead of the Arsenal Match too. Predicted Arsenal lineup:Raya; Timber, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori; Rice, Lewis-Skelly, Odegaard; Saka, Eze; Gyokeres. Viktor Gyokeres (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images) They have taken nine points from their opening five games and possess one of the best defensive records in the division, so this is unlikely to be straightforward. History, however, heavily favours Arsenal. The Gunners have won their last eight meetings with Leeds and scored nine unanswered goals against them across the two league fixtures last season. More importantly, Arteta will demand a reaction following the Brighton defeat. Arsenal had looked in control of their season before that afternoon, but the 3-0 loss was a reminder that simply turning up is never enough in the Premier League. With Liverpool away coming next, dropping more points at home would immediately increase the pressure. I expect Leeds to make Arsenal work for it and their unbeaten record suggests they are unlikely to collapse easily. However, with Saka and Odegaard available, Eze given an opportunity from the left and Gyokeres returning in goalscoring form, Arsenal should have enough attacking quality to respond. title: Veteran Corporate Exec Gale V. King To Be Honored At The ELC Recognition Gala - - Black Enterprise
content: Gale V. King will receive The ELC’s 2026 Heritage Award, recognizing her more than 36 years of corporate leadership, board service, and community impact. Gale V. King, a veteran corporate executive and longtime advocate for leadership development, will receive The Executive Leadership Council’s 2026 Alvaro L. Martins Heritage Award, recognizing a career spanning more than 36 years in business, corporate governance, and community service. The award will be presented Oct. 30 at The ELC Recognition Gala held at the Gaylord National Resort & Convention Center in National Harbor, Maryland. The honor comes as the organization celebrates its 40th anniversary and its longstanding work to expand opportunities for Black executives. King previously served as executive vice president and chief administrative officer of Nationwide, where she oversaw human resources, corporate real estate, corporate security, aviation, and diversity, equity, and inclusion. In that role, she advised the company’s CEO, board, and executive leadership team on organizational culture, employee experience, and business performance. “Gale has spent her career doing the work that lasts: building strong organizations, developing leaders and creating opportunities for others to rise,” said Michael C. Hyter, president and CEO of The Executive Leadership Council, in a statement. “Her leadership has touched companies, boardrooms, communities and The ELC itself. During our 40th anniversary year, it is especially meaningful to recognize someone who has given so much of her leadership to the institution and to the people coming behind her.” The Heritage Award is named for Alvaro L. Martins, one of the ELC’s founding members and its first president and CEO. It recognizes individuals whose leadership and service have helped create opportunities for future generations of executives. King, who received the Barbara Graves Legacy Award at the 2020 BLACK ENTERPRISE Women of Power Summit, chaired The ELC’s board of directors from 2022 to 2024. She currently serves on the boards of AutoZone and Unum Group, extending her influence across corporate governance and business leadership. Her career also reflects a commitment to education and philanthropy. King established endowed scholarships at the University of Florida and Santa Fe College and supports initiatives in addressing homelessness and senior care. Her previous recognitions include the University of Florida Distinguished Alumna Award, YWCA Woman of Power, and National Urban League Woman of Power. Founded in 1986, the ELC is marking four decades of developing executives and strengthening the pipeline of Black business leadership. Its programs span multiple career stages, from helping scholars prepare to enter the workforce to developing midcareer managers and preparing executives for corporate board service. title: Winners and losers from Heat’s second preseason game v. Pelicans - Hot Hot Hoops
content: The Miami Heat are getting slowly, but surely getting ramped up as the Oct. 21 season opener approaches. They concluded their second preseason game on Thursday — a 128-118 win over the Pelicans — with the starters playing in just the first half. Skinny: I didn’t include Antetokounmpo in the preseason opener because it felt fairly obvious. I couldn’t omit him for two straight games. Antetokounmpo tallied a game-high 18 points with four rebounds, four assists and one steal in 18 minutes. He shot 8-of-13 from the floor, with all of his makes coming in the paint. Per status quo, Antetokounmpo dominated in transition and is averaging 13.5 points on 67.6 percent true shooting. He’s been everything as advertised — and then some. Skinny: Conwell, the Heat’s No. 37 overall draft choice, still hasn’t gotten off the ground quite yet. He missed all four of his attempts in Thursday’s win and is 0-for-6 so far in preseason. He’s had difficulty not only finding where he wants to get off his shot, but his balance when he does. This is not a long-term worry, as I expect him to adjust as time passes. Skinny: Mitchell has been outstanding this preseason — especially on Thursday. He finished with nine points and seven assists — to just one turnover — in 20 minutes. He is pushing the rock at every opportunity, spearheading the Heat’s transition attack. He’s also been a bulldog at the point-of-attack. It may look chaotic, but Mitchell’s been in full control on both ends of the floor. Skinny: It’s difficult to be a “loser” in games you don’t play — but that’s part of the reason why Goldin is. This was a big preseason for him to reassure why he’s a two-way player. He has just six points and one rebound to his name through two games and was a DNP-CD on Thursday. Skinny: What allowed Gardner to make the roster last season was his energy in defense. That’s exactly what he’s shown so far this preseason, scoring 11 points on 3-of-5 shooting from deep with four rebounds, four assists and three steals against New Orleans. You have to be aware of Gardner at all times. Beyond that, you have to respect his shooting, which could be a real asset if he gets any run in the rotation. Skinny: The Heat have an intriguing point guard in the pipeline, and his name is Tre Donaldson. The 22-year-old rookie signed with Miami at the conclusion of the 2026 NBA Draft, and has been nothing but impressive since. Through two preseason games, Donaldson’s averaging 9.0 points and 2.5 assists on 46.2/33.3/66.7 shooting splits. He’s not fazed by ball pressure, makes quick reads and defends at a respectable level. I’m a complete buyer in his long-term outcome. It is clear that Miami’s biggest strength this year will be defense. It should be one of the top 5 teams, at minimum. Furthermore, I believe Miami’s offense will also be a strength. The team has a variety of offensive weapons. If I were to project potential scoring averages this season for each player, depending on minutes played, they would probably be as follows: I know Miami won’t average 150+ ppg. Nonetheless, I do believe if Miami’s defense can consistently keep opponents to under 110 ppg, the team has the potential to win 55 or more games this season. title: Matt Hanson Helped Develop the QR V-PRi. Can It Help Him to Another Top-10 Kona Finish? - Slowtwitch News
content: Matt Hanson might be renowned for his incredible running – he ran 2:28:03 at Challenge Roth last year and his three marathon splits at IRONMAN races this year include a 2:34:49 (New Zealand – third), 2:31:50 (Texas – 11th) and 2:30:59 (Sweden – seventh) – but the veteran racer is always looking to improve his bike splits in order to utilize that run for a top finish. Hanson’s best Kona performance here in Kona came the last time the men raced here on the Big Island, when he finished 10th thanks to the day’s second-fastest run split behind Patrick Lange. The new bar saves weight thanks to its 100% carbon fiber design. Every second will truly count for Hanson on Saturday – he’s currently sitting second in the IRONMAN Pro Series standings behind Kristian Blummenfelt. title: How I Got Here: Olena V. Ripnick-O’Farrell ’14 - Columbia Law School
content: Olena V. Ripnick-O'Farrell ’14 is global copyright counsel at ByteDance, a multinational technology company that develops AI models and operates global platforms, including TikTok, that cut across commerce, content, entertainment, and enterprise. I counsel at the intersection of copyright and AI, which means I think about novel issues of copyright law day in and day out. It’s my dream job—focusing solely on copyright is what I’ve always wanted to do in my legal career. My role requires agility, and, much like myself, it doesn’t fit neatly into any box. I’m a U.S. copyright law expert with a deep knowledge of EU and U.K. copyright law, and my practice over the past decade has been a tapestry of litigation, product counseling, and commercial transactions. At ByteDance, I blend substantive knowledge with practical experience to support the development of our AI models and advise internal stakeholders on novel and complex issues of copyright law. I couldn’t think of a role better suited for me. My brain seeks novelty while at the same time craving complexity and deep thinking, and grappling with legal questions for which there are no clear answers and counseling across multiple workstreams brings me joy. I’m on an all-female team for the first time in my legal career, and my teammates are some of the sharpest attorneys I’ve ever worked with. I’m so proud to be a part of this group. This is also the first time in my career where my practice is focused purely on copyright. It’s rare for an IP attorney to be able to specialize like this, and, like most, my previous practice included trademark and right of publicity. I’m indebted to Jeff Cunard, a former Debevoise partner with whom I remain in touch, for enabling me to develop my copyright practice as an associate. If he hadn’t supported me in doing so, the doors that opened and led me to my current role would have remained firmly shut. Professor Jane Ginsburg. I fell in love with copyright law on the very first day of her introductory copyright course. Jane is incredibly knowledgeable and passionate about this subject, and she’s so thoughtful in considering these complex issues. After taking this course, I ended up taking every copyright-related course that Columbia Law offered—including Jane’s elective on international copyright law, which remains relevant in my practice today—and I also served as her research assistant. One of the most exciting things about copyright law is that there aren’t many bright-line rules or clear-cut answers. It’s an evolving space, and the issues I advise on are constantly on my mind, even outside of working hours. Some of my best thinking happens when I’m not at my desk, often on the weekends or when I’m outdoors. To be honest, my passion for this subject probably exceeds what is healthy or typical, but I’m fine with that. I’ve always been interested in legal issues relating to gender equality and the LGBTQ+ community. During my time at the Law School, I was on the staff of the Columbia Journal of Gender and Law, and I served as the vice president of Columbia OutLaws. I also held internships with Immigration Equality and the ACLU’s LGBTQ & HIV Project. Visibility matters. I’m a queer, neurodivergent woman from a rural town in the Catskills. I’ve never had anyone like me to look up to as I have navigated my legal career. Neurodivergence—along with mental health conditions and other disabilities—remains highly stigmatized in the legal profession. There’s an irony here because many neurodivergent traits, such as hyperfocus under pressure, pattern recognition and issue spotting, rules-based system-oriented thinking, and creative problem solving, are significant strengths in practicing law. Each day I choose to be open about my identity, knowing the risk that this entails. I want things to be even a little bit less challenging for those who come next, and my advocacy comes in many forms. I exist openly. I educate others about neurodiversity and neuroinclusive best practices. I assist neurodivergent individuals in navigating the ADA [Americans with Disabilities Act] accommodation process, which can be overwhelming for those who struggle with executive function. And I regularly counsel neurodivergent law students and associates navigating the legal profession. First, keep going. Persevere. Ask for feedback, and learn from your mistakes. Grit and a growth mindset are the most important traits you can develop in any profession. Second, your health is your wealth. You must prioritize it over everything else because no one else will. This perspective is critical, and it’s one that I wish I had had earlier on in my career. title: Confirmed Lineups: Germany W v Australia W - Yahoo Sports
content: Germany and Australia have confirmed their starting lineups for Friday's friendly in Karlsruhe, with both sides looking to make the most of their first match of the international break. Germany head into the match after finishing top of their World Cup qualifying group, while Australia continue preparations following their run to the final of the 2026 AFC Women's Asian Cup. Sam Kerr captains the Matildas, leading an attacking lineup that includes Caitlin Foord and Hayley Raso. Mackenzie Arnold starts in goal, with Steph Catley, Alanna Kennedy's defensive counterpart, Clare Wheeler and Kaitlyn Torpey among the players tasked with keeping Germany at bay. Emily van Egmond joins Wheeler in midfield, while Ellie Carpenter provides another experienced option. Alanna Sayer also earns a starting role, giving her an opportunity to impress against European opposition. Australia will be without Mary Fowler, who withdrew from the squad for personal reasons. Her absence leaves the Matildas without one of their creative attacking options that will inevitably end up putting added responsibility on Kerr, Foord and Raso to create chances. Australia starting XI: Arnold (GK), Heatley, Wheeler, Catley, Torpey, Foord, Van Egmond, Raso, Sayer, Kerr (C), Carpenter. Germany will be captained by Janina Minge, with regular skipper Giulia Gwinn unavailable after suffering an ankle ligament injury while playing for Bayern Munich. Ena Mahmutovic starts in goal, behind a defence featuring Camilla Küver, Minge and Wamser. Sjoeke Nüsken and Elisa Senß add experience through the middle, while Klara Bühl and Jule Brand provide attacking threat. Melissa Kössler and the young Zicai also feature in the starting lineup, giving Germany a chance to assess different options during the international window. For head coach Christian Wück, the match is the first of two tests this break, with Germany also set to face Japan on October 13. Germany starting XI: Mahmutovic (GK), Küver, Minge (C), Nüsken, Wamser, Zicai, Kett, Kössler, Bühl, Senß, Brand. The two sides last met in October 2024 when Australia came from behind to win 2–1 in Duisburg. Friday's meeting gives Germany the chance to respond on home soil, while Australia will look to build on their recent performances and continue developing their options ahead of next year's World Cup. With both nations already qualified for Brazil 2027, the focus in Karlsruhe will be on how the teams perform, which combinations click and who takes their opportunity to make an impression.

title: Joe V’s Smart Shop Opening Not One But Two Locations in Greater Houston - WhatNow
content:
Joe V’s Smart Shop is working on not one, but two openings for the Greater Houston community and its visitors. The discount grocer is expected to open near the City Park community and in Humble, according to the Houston Business Journal. The brand’s website confirms that the upcoming locations will be at 1227 W. Orem Drive near Highway 288 and 19611 US-59 near Interstate 69, with plans to open both in 2027. “With work already underway, the 57,000-square-foot stores are expected to open next year – with the Humble location in early 2027 and the Orem Drive store in late 2027,” the company’s website reads. “Joe V’s Smart Shop is an innovative price format focused on offering the freshest, highest-quality products at the best prices including fresh produce, in-store cut meats, breads and tortillas made in store, and sushi made daily.” In addition, the two new Joe V’s Smart Shop locations will also be the first to offer H-E-B South Flo Pizza. “The freshly made pizzas will be handcrafted in-house daily as an available grab-and-go meal option,” the H-E-B Newsroom blog reads. “These locations will also offer Home Delivery to serve even more customers throughout the community and surrounding neighborhoods.” What Now Houston reached out to H-E-B Chief Operating Officer Roxanne Orsak to find out more about the exciting two new additions to the community. Unfortunately, we did not hear back by the time of this publication. “At Joe V’s Smart Shop by H-E-B, we’ve always had one goal in mind: Keep prices low and quality high,” the Joe V’s Smart Shop website reads. “We work hard to do this everyday. Each of our stores carry many of the high-quality, fresh products H-E-B is known for, at even lower prices. That’s smart shopping. That’s Joe V’s Smart Shop by H-E-B.” Orsak is widely credited as the executive who originally came up with the discount concept. She wanted to build a lean, high-efficiency store format specifically tailored to help budget-conscious families. Joe Villarreal, the Director of Operations and Innovation for Joe V’s and who the brand is named after, worked directly alongside Orsak to design and develop the business model. His career journey—starting as an H-E-B night janitor in the 1980s and rising to corporate leadership—inspired the chain’s name and its mascot. The brand launched in the summer of 2010 in Houston, emerging in the wake of the Great Recession to serve price-conscious households on tight budgets. H-E-B designed the stores to offer high-quality fresh produce, meat, and bakery goods alongside an efficient product selection of fewer than 10,000 SKUs (stock-keeping units), balancing discount pricing with a clean, upbeat shopping environment. After operating exclusively as a Houston-area staple for over a decade, Joe V’s opened its first DFW location in Dallas in June 2024. The chain now operates multiple successful stores across the Houston and Dallas-Fort Worth metroplexes. There are now 14 Joe V’s Smart Shop locations operating in the United States, all of which are located in Texas, with 11 stores in the Greater Houston area. Joe V’s Smart Shop is anticipated to open at 1227 W. Orem Drive near Highway 288 in early 2027 and at 19611 US-59 near Interstate 69 in late 2027. (This is a developing story. title: Ipswich Town v Fulham: Key stats and talking points - Yahoo Sports
content: BBC Sport examines some of the key themes before Saturday's match (15:00 BST), with Fulham visiting Ipswich looking for their first league win of the season. Ipswich players not called up by their countries spent part of the international break at a warm-weather training camp in Spain, which culminated in a 1-0 win over Espanyol in a behind-closed-doors friendly on 2 October. The Tractor Boys have yet to keep a competitive clean sheet under Gary O'Neil, but will hope shutting out the La Liga outfit can provide a springboard towards greater defensive solidity. Only Chelsea have conceded more top-flight goals than the Blues, who are also among the league's worst sides for shots faced, big chances faced and duel success rate. O'Neil made two changes to his backline for the defeat at Everton last time out. Summer signing Kjell Scherpen made way for Christian Walton in goal, while Abdoul Ouattara replaced Jacob Greaves in defence, allowing captain Dara O'Shea to move from right-back to his preferred position at centre-back. Those alterations did not quite pay off, with the Blues beaten 1-0 on Merseyside, but they showed plenty of attacking endeavour, even after being reduced to 10 men for the final 23 minutes. That performance will give the newly promoted side confidence as they target a third Premier League win of the season. It took them 19 games to reach that tally during their most recent top-flight campaign in 2024-25. Fulham are one of three clubs still searching for their first Premier League win, but back-to-back draws against Liverpool and Manchester United have provided encouragement for new boss Alvaro Arbeloa. His side came close to beating United, only for a deflected Matheus Cunha strike to level the scores in the 89th minute. Arbeloa was outspoken in his criticism of referee Peter Bankes after the match, complaining that "every decision" had gone United's way. He has since been charged with misconduct by the Football Association. The Cottagers now begin a run of three consecutive games against the three promoted clubs, and the Spaniard is likely to come under pressure if he is still without a victory at the end of that sequence. This is only the fourth time Fulham have failed to win any of their opening five top-flight games. The last time it happened, in 2020-21, they went on to be relegated.

title: Sunderland v Brighton: Key stats and talking points - Yahoo Sports
content: Brighton look to continue the excellent form they showed prior to the international break against a Sunderland side who have won just once so far this season. BBC Sport takes a look at some of the key themes going into the fixture at Stadium of Light. How Brighton must wish the international break had come at a different time. Their final act of a brilliant September was to dismantle champions Arsenal with a performance that chairman Tony Bloom said was "arguably the best" in the club's 125-year history. Their stunning run of form led to the Seagulls rightfully being rewarded as Fabian Hurzeler was named September's manager of the month and Pascal Gross player of the month, while captain Lewis Dunk took the honours for best goal after his dipping rocket against Coventry City. The Premier League's leading scorers sit top or near the top of almost every major attracting metric so far this season and average a whopping 3.2 goals per game. Their past two league matches have ended in an aggregate scoreline of 8-0 and they will be aiming to record three games in a row in the competition without conceding for only the second time. In total, they have kept five clean sheets in their eight matches this season. But will any of their momentum be taken away by having three weeks off? The irony, of course, is that fixtures now come at a frightening rate, with seven matches in 21 days as their Conference League commitments really kick in. But Bloom believes the club have more than enough to cope. "We've got a great squad and the biggest depth we've ever had," he said. "We don't have ceilings and we can finish high in the Premier League. Absolutely, if we have a really good season, we have a realistic chance of finishing in the top five." While Brighton cursed the arrival of the international break, Sunderland will have been relieved for a break after the rigours of facing Arsenal and Manchester City on back-to-back weekends. Their 5-3 defeat at Etihad Stadium will go down as one of the games of the season, with Brian Brobbey becoming only the sixth player to score a Premier League hat-trick in defeat and only the fourth man to score a treble against the side starting the day top of the Premier League. However, the Black Cats suffered a big blow when the striker suffered a minor hamstring injury playing in the Netherlands' draw with Germany and he has joined fellow key men Dan Ballard and Habib Diarra on the sidelines. Head coach Regis le Bris will need them all back firing as soon as possible because, like Brighton, they are entering a punishing period of matches and also play seven times by the end of October. Le Bris, who celebrated 100 matches in charge of the Black Cats in their defeat by City, has seen his side win just one of their opening five league matches, but at least the top two are now out of the way. They actually had a whopping xG of 4.15 compared to City's 2.72, but Brobbey's hat-trick in that game accounts for half their six league goals and they have underperformed in front of goal. Sunderland have actually only been ahead for 3.9% of their game time this season, all of which came in the final 19 minutes of their win over Fulham. Le Bris, who has lavished praise on Brighton in the build-up to this game, says his side have a "tough test" if they are to celebrate what would be only a second top-flight victory over the Seagulls, and their first since in May 1982.

title: Chelsea v Bournemouth: Key stats and talking points - Yahoo Sports
content: Chelsea seek a return to form at the expense of Bournemouth, who are winless in the league this season as well as in the past nine meetings between the clubs – although the three most recent occasions all ended in draws. Widely lauded after opening the season with two entertaining wins, Chelsea have nosedived to mid-table and eight points off the top three games later. "We have dropped our consistency and our competitive mentality," bemoaned head coach Xabi Alonso in the wake of the 3-0 loss at Brentford immediately prior to the international break. That defeat was Chelsea's 11th of 2026 in the league, already one more than in the entirety of last year. Chelsea's defensive shortcomings have been much discussed. They have faced the most shots on target (32), let in a league-high 12 goals and could become only the third team in Premier League history to concede twice or more in each of their opening six games of a season, after Everton in 1994-95 and Derby County in 2000-01. Furthermore, the Blues' current run of 21 league fixtures without a clean sheet is their longest since a club record 31-match streak between 1960 and 1961. Nonetheless, Chelsea's attacking potency means they are providing great entertainment, for neutral observers at least. Their top-flight games have produced an unrivalled 22 goals and they are just the 10th side to both score and concede double figures across their first five Premier League matches in a season. Each of the previous three, beginning with Chelsea themselves in 2019-20, went on to finish in the top four. It has also been a curious start to 2026-27 for Bournemouth, who won on their European debut away to Real Sociedad and are through to the fourth round of the Carabao Cup – but remain without a victory in the league despite only trailing for 45 minutes this season. They now face a run of nine games in 30 days without key midfielder Alex Scott, who was the subject of a failed £64m bid from Chelsea in the summer. He gave an assured display on his first senior England start against Croatia last weekend but suffered a thigh muscle injury during that 7-0 win. "He is good in everything, and to miss a player who is good in everything is a challenge," admitted Bournemouth head coach Marco Rose. That assessment of Scott's importance is borne out by the fact he ranks in the Premier League top five this season for a variety of metrics, including winning possession, fouls won and total distance covered.

title: Arsenal v Leeds United: Key stats and talking points - Yahoo Sports
content: Having had three weeks to stew on their loss to Brighton, Arsenal will be itching to get going in the Premier League again. Unbeaten Leeds United are their opponents in the Premier League on Saturday (12:30 BST) at Emirates Stadium. The Gunners were uncharacteristically out of sorts at Amex Stadium before the international break, as their perfect start to the season was ended in spectacular fashion by a 3-0 defeat. Mikel Arteta, who signed a new contract this week, will want to see his side bounce back like champions. Leeds will pose a big challenge, though. After a summer of solid transfer business, they have started the campaign well, winning two and drawing three of their first five fixtures. Daniel Farke's side have the joint-best defensive record in the league too and will fancy their chances of springing a surprise. The 3-0 reverse at Brighton was Arsenal's biggest Premier League defeat since May 2023 against the same opposition. Arteta said it was a "big lesson", so supporters will be expecting a response. In fairness to the Gunners, the nature of the defeat was out of sync with the defensive standards they have set under the current head coach. They only lost by more than one goal once in the whole of last season, against Manchester City in the Carabao Cup final. So how do they do it? They need to take more care in possession to start. Against the Seagulls, the Gunners lost possession in their own final third nine times, which was the most for them since December 2023. Leeds are second for pressed sequences in the Premier League so far this season, with 63, and will fancy their chances of potentially pinching possession back in dangerous areas too. While so far this season teams with less than 50% of possession have won more games than teams with 50% of the ball, Arsenal have pivoted towards a controlled style of play with the ball. In Leeds, they do at least have historically accommodating opponents. Arsenal have won nine of their past 10 Premier League games against the Whites, including the past seven by an aggregate score of 24-5. Farke's side can go to the Emirates with nothing to fear, though, and will take confidence from the robustness of the squad they have assembled. They have been superb at the back, with goalkeeper James Trafford and defender Tarik Muharemovic adding extra steel since their summer arrivals. As a team, they have limited their opponents to just 0.09 xG per shot, a tally only the Gunners can better with 0.08. Where Leeds may also be able to match Arsenal is from attacking set-pieces. They lead the Premier League for the percentage of their shots (46.7%) and xG (41.0%) which have come from non-penalty set-pieces, with three of their seven goals coming from dead-ball situations. Arsenal scored a massive 29 goals from set-pieces on their way to the title last season, with their inswinging corners a defining feature of their play. But five games in, Arteta's side have yet to score from a dead-ball situation.

title: Man Utd v Tottenham: Key stats and talking points - Yahoo Sports
content: Both Manchester United and Tottenham have had underwhelming starts to the season, leading to the pressure growing both head coaches. BBC Sport takes a look at some of the key themes going into Saturday's fixture at Old Trafford. Seven games into the season and the only victories Manchester United have enjoyed have come against newly promoted Ipswich Town and Champions League debutants Sabah. Their tally of just five points from five league matches represents their joint worst start to a Premier League season, along with the 2014-15 campaign. As a result, the pressure has been steadily building on Michael Carrick - though he has lost just five of 24 matches since taking over in January. A sift through United's statistics produces some eye-catching numbers, with their 113 shots and 182 touches in the opposition box both top-flight highs. But they have failed to capitalise on these attacking endeavours and Carrick's tactical shift to a more possession-based game needs to reap dividends sooner rather than later to get the doubters off his back. Historically, Tottenham at home has been a dream fixture for the Red Devils. The 25 defeats they have inflicted on Spurs at Old Trafford is the second-most away losses a Premier League side has suffered at a venue, after Everton's 26 at Arsenal. But Tottenham had enjoyed the upper hand of late - until United ended their eight-match unbeaten run with a 2-0 victory in February. It has been a long three weeks for bottom-of-the-table Spurs to ponder a start to the campaign in which they have failed to win any of their opening five league matches and took 446 minutes to score a top-flight goal. In the wake of their defeat by Aston Villa, head coach Roberto de Zerbi pulled no punches as the scale of his task to shed the club's losing culture becomes starker. "It's difficult to explain because, in my career, 14 years as a coach, I've never seen one team like us - so fragile, so inconsistent," he said. This fragility he talks of is nothing new and is something the previous incumbents of the Tottenham hot seat have also had to wrestle with. Spurs have failed to win any of their past 48 matches (37 in the Premier League) when they have conceded the opening goal. Meanwhile, their tally of 18 points won in 2026 is the lowest of any ever-present side. An increasingly exasperated De Zerbi has tinkered heavily with his team selection to try to change their fortunes - the 13 he has made to his starting line-ups across the first five matches is more than any other top-flight side, while the 26 starts he has given to players who didn't play a game for them last season is nine higher than any other team. But all the alterations are yet to have the desired effect and Spurs are the only Premier League side yet to lead a match this season. If they fail to win at Old Trafford it will only be the fourth time in their history that they have not won any of their opening six league games of a season, following the 1912-13 (first 12 games), 2008-09 (eight) and 1955-56 (six) campaigns.

title: What’s New in New Source Review? EPA’s Title V Rule Adds to a Growing List of NSR Developments - JDSupra
content:
Generally speaking, the CAA’s Title V Operating Permit program is a vehicle to compile and assure compliance with “applicable requirements” that other CAA programs impose on the source; it is not an opportunity to substantively reconsider the requirements themselves. That distinction is important because Title V has unique federal oversight tools that can disrupt permitting, including mechanisms for EPA to object to the issuance of a facility’s state-issued Title V operating permit and cause the permit to be modified, revoked, or terminated. Title V also establishes a related process for members of the public to petition EPA for such an objection, with exceptionally tight deadlines that can quickly force an EPA response. EPA’s final rule codifies an approach the agency had developed in a pair of Title V orders, Hunter and Big River Steel, both issued in October 2017. Under that approach, when an NSR permit is issued subject to requirements for public notice, opportunity for public comment, and opportunity for judicial review, the resulting terms and conditions are the NSR-related “applicable requirements” under Title V and cannot be revisited during the Title V permitting process. That principle extends to NSR permit content, such as Best Available Control Technology (BACT) determinations, and whether major or minor NSR applies. Limited Title V review remains available where NSR requirements have not been conclusively established, including where no NSR permit was issued, or the requisite opportunities for public participation and judicial review were not available. Separately, but also notably, the final rule also clarifies that the General Duty Clause of CAA Section 112(r)(1) is not an “applicable requirement” according to EPA’s statutory interpretation of Title V. However, accident-prevention requirements under CAA Section 112(r)(7) remain subject to Title V’s definition of “applicable requirements.” The Title V final rule on “applicable requirements” is the latest in a series of recent developments related to NSR. The changes and proposed changes are particularly relevant to companies planning to develop data centers, onsite generation, or to undertake other major capital projects, where air permitting requirements can often affect construction schedules. EPA guidance and rulemakings, federal court decisions, pending legislation, and enforcement litigation are addressing when NSR applies, how sources calculate emissions, when construction may begin, and how NSR disputes should be resolved: NSR developments are not limited to EPA. In Congress, several pieces of proposed legislation would alter aspects of NSR permitting. For example, the House Energy and Commerce Committee has reported out: In the courts, NSR enforcement litigation remains consequential. Earlier this year in United States v. EES Coke Battery, LLC, the Eastern District of Michigan imposed a $100 million civil penalty and injunctive relief for NSR violations, and held not just the plant owner liable, but also several other affiliated entities liable as “operators” due to the high degree of control they exhibited over the facility. United States v. EES Coke Battery, LLC, 820 F. Supp. 3d 600 (E.D. Mich. 2026). Given the stakes for project timing and the highly fluid NSR landscape, companies must consider how these recent and ongoing developments affect applicability analyses, construction sequencing, offset acquisition, compliance documentation, and overall air permitting strategy. And these relatively recent developments capture only part of the broader range of NSR issues that may arise, including source-determination questions such as common control and adjacency, project aggregation and “circumvention,” and the scope of what constitutes a major modification. In the case of EPA’s recent rule clarifying “applicable requirements” under Title V, a principal benefit is that it formally limits opportunities to use the Title V process as a “second bite at the apple” for NSR determinations—some of which, as in Hunter, may be decades old. At the same time, the rule does not eliminate other avenues to challenge or enforce NSR requirements. By expressly limiting the extent to which underlying NSR determinations can later be revisited through Title V, the rule may instead place greater importance on strategic decisions made during the initial preconstruction permitting process, when public participation, agency review, and potential litigation can have immediate consequences for project schedules. Companies planning new facilities or modifications to existing ones should therefore consider not only whether and how NSR applies, but also how best to develop a defensible permitting record at the outset. title: Steelers running back a must-start in fantasy football v. Colts defense - Yahoo Sports
content: ESPN fantasy football analyst Eric Moody is bullish on Steelers running back Jaylen Warren this week against the Indianapolis Colts' defense. Warren will enter Sunday's game with 309 rushing yards -- the 10th-most among running backs -- and he's averaging a hefty 5.6 yards per attempt. The Colts' defense, meanwhile, ranks 28th in yards per rush allowed. So naturally, starting Warren seems like the move to make in Week 5. "Steelers RB Jaylen Warren has 20 touches in each of the past two games and at least 15 fantasy points in both with Rico Dowdle (toe) out," Moody wrote. "Warren now faces a Colts defense that ranks 30th in run stop win rate and has allowed the seventh-most rushing yards per game. Indianapolis has also allowed the fourth-most receiving yards per game to RBs." To Moody's final point, Warren has also been fairly active in the passing game, totaling 19 targets through four games, while averaging 11.0 yards per catch. title: Upbeat Technology’s Bluemag Pi Pairs RISC-V Processors and AI Inference for Advanced Flight Control - Embedded Computing Design
content:
Upbeat Technology launched the Bluemag Pi, a sensor-integrated AI flight controller built for long-endurance fixed-wing aircraft, commercial multirotor drones, and unmanned surface vessels. The solution utilizes Upbeat's UP301 system-on-chip, combining SiFive's E3 and E2 RISC-V processor cores in a dual-core architecture built for flight-critical applications. Bluemag Pi provides engineers with a single, reliable board built for both flight-critical control and AI inference. "Flight control is one of the toughest tests for any processor architecture, hard real-time guarantees, built-in redundancy, and now onboard AI, all on a tight power budget. Leveraging both SiFive’s E3 and E2 Essential RISC-V CPU IP Complexes lets Upbeat dedicate one core to flight-critical control and the other to AI and system tasks, without either one compromising the other. Bluemag Pi proves RISC-V is ready for more than edge AI, it's ready for the real-time, safety-critical systems that autonomous flight depends on," said Martyn Stroeve, Vice President, SiFive. To improve awareness and consistency, the UP301's multicore architecture splits time-critical flight tasks from communication, navigation, and system-management functions. Supporting advanced flight operations, the board offers generous RAM, nonvolatile storage, hardware floating-point capability, timers, direct memory access (DMA), and interrupt resources. Bluemag Pi runs Apache NuttX real-time operating system and is compatible with open-source flight-control stacks, including PX4, ArduPilot, and Betaflight. By pairing two independent inertial measurement units (IMUs), a barometer, and dual global navigation satellite system (GNSS) receivers with sensor-fusion software, the Bluemag Pi constantly cross-checks data resulting in trustworthy altitude, attitude, and velocity estimates even if a single sensor drifts or fails. The board uses a standard MAVLink radio link to transmit telemetry to a ground station or companion computer while accepting input from common remote-control receivers, and drives motors through an integrated four-in-one electronic speed controller for precise throttle response. Additional interfaces support expansion sensors and peripherals. Onboard storage continuously logs flight data for diagnostics, tuning, and post-flight analysis. According to the press release, Bluemag Pi is available as a standard board that fully supports secondary development, allowing engineers to implement their own custom flight algorithms. Customers wanting to design their own proprietary carrier boards can purchase the UP301 chip directly. The UP301 can support manual, stabilized, altitude-hold, position-hold, mission, return-to-home, and autonomous flight modes. Chad Cox is the Production Editor at Embedded Computing Design. title: Liverpool v Manchester City: The Conflicting Feelings Of A Fan - The Anfield Wrap
content: by Dan Morgan | Oct 9, 2026 | app, Dan Morgan's Column, Featured Writing, Footie | 0 comments Should I be so vexed by the events of the past two weeks that I bounce into Anfield on Sunday? I’m far from it. My bounce is more of a trudge. I’ll rock up and see what greets me, because for the first time in a long time I’m uncertain. Manchester City’s drama is now my business. All of our business. We all need to read the statements, listen to the legal experts, and shake our heads at Andy Burnham’s inescapable Evertonianism. A lot of people welcome this into their lives. They are fuelled by the verdict and can’t wait for Sunday. They’re right to feel incensed and conned by City’s ownership. They should be in disbelief at those encouraging City to burn the Premier League to the ground rather than succumb to sanctions. Eventually Burnham, City supporters, and whoever else is still directly or indirectly fighting their corner, will see that this issue poses an existential threat to football in this country and that they should rally behind saving it. I genuinely believe this is where we end up here. But, back to me. The fella who cannot extrapolate any joy, rage or general sense of feeling towards this entire thing. I’m tired of it. Tired by it. It’s excruciating for one key reason: That’s where I’m at my most irrational but also my most informed. Football is my wheelhouse. Getting to see the best on the planet do it in our corner of earth is a genuine gift. If Sunday was about two of the best sides in the country going at it without any of City’s discrepancies attached, you had best believe I’d be motivated. Best believe I’d be bouncing. The thing I’m pissed off about the most is that City’s guilty verdict makes a sham of the rivalry. It taints some of the greatest games of football I’ve seen. It makes me more angry that the legacy of what I watched is now disingenuous. Liverpool did nothing wrong. The memory of Jürgen Klopp’s team has warmed considerably in recent days. That they and everyone else have had their name dragged into such a shitshow is regrettable. I wanted City to be pure. I wanted to be beaten by the best side the Premier League has ever seen, with a manager who will go down as one of the all-time greats. I want them to be assembled fairly, because even though it hurts looking back, you can still shrug at how lucky you were to see an elite rivalry in which both sides clearly drove each other. There’s been some recent Anfield Wrap shows about what we want from our football club. I’ve enjoyed them and been reminded of how complex and entangled the concept of togetherness is when engaging in supporting a major club. The past two weeks have challenged me to think about what I want from football. I want to see the best players on the planet, but at what cost? Diplomatic threats and the potential liquidation of the football clubs they acquire? Surely there’s a middle ground that exists between having the best league in the world and supporters and governments being financially blackmailed as a result. It feels too risky, even if the reward is trophies and success. Ultimately, I just want to watch the game and ponder how Liverpool can be great again without feeling the need to shower every time I do. I suppose that’s what made Klopp’s teams so special. They were human to a fault. They oozed authenticity and honesty. From lactate tests to lie detectors, his Liverpool team passed with flying colours. So, what does this all mean for Sunday? There’s a world where City take a game away from Liverpool through bad officiating, a lack of fit players on our part, or them just being better. How much any City result is accepted by football is the question nobody can answer. How do Anfield, Villa Park, The City Ground and everywhere else react when a sense of darker forces being at play is now proven? This – like the entire episode – feels too big to ponder. I don’t want to think about commercial revenues in a football stadium. I want to encourage my team and vilify the opposition and referee because football is what matters. I will get behind the lads in Red, as is the minimum requirement for anyone fortunate enough to enter Anfield. As for the opposition, I’m tired, bored and confused by the sight of them already. Worst of all, I’ve got no idea how that leaves me feeling towards a game I’ve been so certain about my entire life. Your email address will not be published. title: Trademark case: Smith v. Airbnb, Inc., USA - Wolters Kluwer
content: The registrant failed to show that his domain name airbnbseo.com was not confusingly similar to Airbnb’s famous mark, or that he acted without a bad faith intent to profit from that mark. The Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed the district court’s dismissal of claims brought under the Anticybersquatting Consumer Protection Act (ACPA) and Arizona common law. After Airbnb successfully obtained a transfer of the disputed domain name airbnbseo.com, its registrant sued to block the transfer. The registrant’s second amended complaint (SAC) did not establish that this domain name was not confusingly similar to AIRBNB, nor that he lacked a bad faith intent to profit from the use of Airbnb’s mark (Smith v. Airbnb, Inc., No. 25-571 (9th Cir. Jul. 8, 2026)). title: Liverpool v Manchester City: Where to Watch, Match Preview, Kick Off Time & More - Yahoo Sports
content: Liverpool return to action this weekend, as they take on a Manchester City side with a lot of eyes on them, following the news surrounding their 115 charges. The big topic going into this game will be about how Man City react on the pitch after being found guilty by the Premier League of 115 breaches of financial rules, with Liverpool one of the sides most affected by these breaches. So with all the pressure being placed on the away side in this fixture, the Reds will be hoping that they can thrive and secure a huge win over their bitter rivals. The last time these two sides met, it produced a thrilling encounter with late goals, red cards and drama until the very end, but it was the Citizens who came out on top. A game in which Liverpool led thanks to a magical free-kick from Dominik Szoboszlai in the 74th minute. City piled on the pressure, amid a title race with Arsenal, and found an equaliser via Bernardo Silva. A penalty would be given in the 93rd minute for Manchester City after Alisson was judged to have fouled Matheus Nunes in the box, in which Erling Haaland clinically finished past the Brazilian goalkeeper to give his side a late winner. The Merseyside club continued to push and forced a stunning stop from Donnarumma late in the game, before Dominik Szoboszlai was sent off for a tussle with Haaland as the pair charged towards the LFC goal. But that would be that, a huge win for City, the final time Pep Guardiola would face the Anfield crowd as City boss, and a hammer blow for Liverpool in a game they led going into the final 10 minutes. Before the international break, Andoni Iraola returned to his former club, Bournemouth, as he looked to bring three points back from the South Coast. And thanks to a goal from Alexander Isak set up again by Cody Gakpo, three points are exactly what Iraola would get as a blunt Bournemouth side was punished for a lack of a clinical edge, with Liverpool winning 1-0. Enzo Maresca's side has been in fine form at the start of the season, with an unbeaten league season and the Champions League, as well as advancing in the Carabao Cup. Despite the departure of Pep Guardiola in the summer, it clearly has not affected the team's performances so far this campaign. But now that we have had a three-week break from club football, and the news of their 115 charges, an away trip to Anfield would not have been what Maresca and his team would have liked upon their return to action.
